system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Seattle, . Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Seattle itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Seattle space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Pioneer Square, Downtown, Capitol Hill, Ballard/Fremont, Georgetown, University District) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Seattle spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Seattle, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Greg Kucera Gallery
galleries.note: Seattle’s leading long-established contemporary gallery, with a nationally recognized roster, sustained art-fair activity and strong museum placement.

galleries.name: James Harris Gallery
galleries.note: A rigorous contemporary program with national and international artists, regular fair participation and substantial institutional attention.

galleries.name: Traver Gallery
galleries.note: Internationally influential in contemporary glass while maintaining a broader sculpture and painting program with major institutional reach.

galleries.name: Winston Wächter Fine Art
galleries.note: A prominent Seattle–New York gallery representing established contemporary artists across painting, photography, sculpture and installation.

galleries.name: Davidson Galleries
galleries.note: One of the country’s important works-on-paper dealers, combining historic print expertise with a substantial contemporary program.

galleries.name: Foster/White Gallery
galleries.note: A durable regional anchor with a broad contemporary roster and particular strength in Northwest painting, sculpture and glass.

galleries.name: Woodside/Braseth Gallery
galleries.note: A historically important Seattle gallery whose long program connects Northwest modernism with successive generations of contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Koplin Del Rio Gallery
galleries.note: Known for technically accomplished figurative and narrative art, with a long record of national exhibitions and institutional placements.

galleries.name: SOIL
galleries.note: Seattle’s most consequential artist-run gallery, sustaining experimental practices and launching many artists who later gained institutional recognition.

galleries.name: Stonington Gallery
galleries.note: A major venue for contemporary Indigenous art of the Pacific Northwest Coast, representing leading carvers, glass artists and multidisciplinary practitioners.

galleries.name: studio e
galleries.note: A closely curated contemporary gallery that has become influential for introducing emerging and mid-career artists to Seattle collectors and institutions.

galleries.name: J. Rinehart Gallery
galleries.note: A well-regarded contemporary program emphasizing distinctive regional voices, material experimentation and sustained artist development.

galleries.name: Roq La Rue Gallery
galleries.note: Internationally known for imaginative realism, pop surrealism and technically refined figurative art, with a loyal global following.

galleries.name: ArtX Contemporary
galleries.note: The successor to ArtXchange Gallery, maintaining a globally minded program centered on diasporic, cross-cultural and socially engaged practices.

galleries.name: Wa Na Wari
galleries.note: A nationally noticed Black arts organization presenting exhibitions, residencies and community programs in a culturally significant neighborhood house.

galleries.name: Gallery 4Culture
galleries.note: King County’s principal public contemporary-art gallery, supporting experimental work by regional artists through exhibitions and commissions.

galleries.name: Photographic Center Northwest
galleries.note: The region’s leading nonprofit photography venue, pairing critically engaged exhibitions with residencies, publications and public education.

galleries.name: ARTS at King Street Station
galleries.note: Seattle’s flagship municipal exhibition space, notable for ambitious artist-led projects and sustained emphasis on communities historically excluded from institutions.

galleries.name: Center on Contemporary Art (CoCA)
galleries.note: A pioneering Seattle contemporary-art nonprofit with decades of experimental exhibitions, installations and artist-centered programming.

galleries.name: TrepanierBaer
galleries.note: A newer gallery with an unusually accomplished roster of established Northwest artists and a polished, institutionally oriented program.

galleries.name: Specialist
galleries.note: A focused contemporary gallery and curatorial platform presenting intellectually ambitious work by emerging and established artists.

galleries.name: Patricia Rovzar Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding commercial gallery with a strong collector base and an established program of contemporary painting, sculpture and mixed media.

galleries.name: ZINC contemporary
galleries.note: A respected contemporary gallery known for vivid figurative, narrative and materially inventive work by regional and national artists.

galleries.name: Jacob Lawrence Gallery
galleries.note: The University of Washington’s principal contemporary-art gallery, connecting visiting artists, research, experimental curating and emerging practices.

galleries.name: Hedreen Gallery
galleries.note: Seattle University’s public contemporary gallery, recognized for research-driven installations, socially engaged projects and adventurous curatorial work.

galleries.name: Mini Mart City Park
galleries.note: An artist-founded cultural center built on a remediated former gas station, combining contemporary exhibitions with environmental and community programming.

galleries.name: Jack Straw New Media Gallery
galleries.note: A distinctive venue for sound art, media installation and interdisciplinary work, supported by a respected residency and production program.

galleries.name: Gallery 110
galleries.note: A durable artist-run gallery providing consistent public exposure for emerging and mid-career contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Shift Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding artist-run cooperative valued for independent programming and direct support of experimental regional practices.

galleries.name: ARTE NOIR
galleries.note: A prominent Black arts and culture organization presenting exhibitions, supporting artists and preserving the Central District’s creative legacy.

galleries.name: Nii Modo
galleries.note: An Indigenous-led gallery and marketplace extending yəhaw̓ Indigenous Creatives’ influential work on visibility, economic opportunity and cultural sovereignty.

galleries.name: Common Area Maintenance
galleries.note: An artist-run workspace and exhibition platform that supports collaborative, experimental and community-oriented contemporary projects.

galleries.name: Mount Analogue
galleries.note: An independent exhibition, publishing and art-book platform known for conceptually adventurous projects and strong ties to artist-led culture.

galleries.name: Forest For The Trees Gallery
galleries.note: The exhibition arm of Seattle’s influential mural and public-art initiative, connecting street-art practices with a permanent gallery context.

galleries.name: Gray Sky Gallery
galleries.note: A contemporary gallery with an accessible regional program spanning abstraction, figuration, photography and mixed media.

galleries.name: Orcas Paley
galleries.note: An artist-run venue presenting idiosyncratic, critically engaged exhibitions by emerging and established contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Frederick Holmes and Company
galleries.note: A polished gallery combining contemporary exhibitions with selected modern and secondary-market material for an established collector audience.

galleries.name: Gallery Mack
galleries.note: A long-running Seattle gallery with a broad roster and particular visibility in painting, sculpture and studio glass.

galleries.name: Steinbrueck Native Gallery
galleries.note: An important commercial platform for contemporary Northwest Coast Indigenous artists, emphasizing knowledgeable representation and cultural context.

galleries.name: Bryan Ohno Gallery
galleries.note: A veteran gallery with a cross-disciplinary program linking contemporary visual art, science, technology and public conversation.

galleries.name: Lynn Hanson Gallery
galleries.note: A well-established venue for contemporary Northwest artists, especially painting, drawing, sculpture and materially focused work.

galleries.name: Columbia City Gallery
galleries.note: A longstanding cooperative gallery and South Seattle cultural anchor supporting diverse regional artists and community exhibitions.

galleries.name: Nepantla Cultural Arts Gallery
galleries.note: A significant Chicano- and Latinx-centered gallery presenting politically engaged contemporary art and building cultural infrastructure in West Seattle.

galleries.name: Martyr Sauce
galleries.note: An independent Black-led art space known for energetic exhibitions, performances and support of artists outside conventional gallery systems.

galleries.name: The Vestibule
galleries.note: An intimate artist-run venue that gives installation, performance and experimental work unusual freedom and close audience engagement.

galleries.name: Oxbow
galleries.note: A Georgetown artist collective and exhibition venue fostering cross-disciplinary projects within one of Seattle’s strongest studio communities.

galleries.name: Base: Experimental Arts + Space
galleries.note: A flexible artist-run venue for experimental exhibitions, performance, movement and other practices poorly served by commercial galleries.

galleries.name: Das Schaufenster
galleries.note: A window-based exhibition space offering continuous public access to concise, experimental installations by local and visiting artists.

galleries.name: Gallery B612
galleries.note: A developing nonprofit contemporary gallery that provides exhibitions, residencies and professional opportunities for emerging artists.

galleries.name: Vermillion Art Gallery and Bar
galleries.note: A durable hybrid gallery and social space that has made contemporary exhibitions unusually accessible to Capitol Hill audiences.

galleries.name: CORE Gallery
galleries.note: An artist-run cooperative sustaining regular solo and group exhibitions in the Tashiro Kaplan arts complex.

galleries.name: Slip Gallery
galleries.note: A small artist-run gallery with a focused emerging-art program and an emphasis on experimentation and dialogue.

galleries.name: Sacred Circle Gallery
galleries.note: United Indians of All Tribes Foundation’s gallery provides an important public platform for contemporary Native artists and cultural continuity.

galleries.name: The Grocery Studios
galleries.note: A neighborhood-based artist space presenting exhibitions, performances and community programs in a converted former grocery store.

galleries.name: Fogue Studios & Gallery
galleries.note: A distinctive gallery and studio community advocating for accomplished older artists who remain underrepresented in the contemporary market.

galleries.name: A/NT Gallery
galleries.note: A long-running nonprofit gallery notable for its open-entry model and broad access for artists outside established commercial networks.

galleries.name: Fantagraphics Bookstore & Gallery
galleries.note: The public gallery of the internationally influential comics publisher, exhibiting major cartoonists, illustrators and artists working across visual narrative.

galleries.name: The Vera Project Gallery
galleries.note: A youth-centered exhibition space that gives emerging artists early curatorial and professional experience within a larger music and arts institution.

galleries.name: Seattle City Hall Gallery
galleries.note: A municipal gallery presenting contemporary work from Seattle’s civic collection alongside exhibitions focused on regional artists and public issues.

galleries.name: Behnke Family Gallery
galleries.note: Cornish College of the Arts’ principal public gallery, presenting visiting artists, faculty projects and emerging contemporary practices.

galleries.name: Phinney Center Gallery
galleries.note: A well-used community gallery that provides sustained public exhibition opportunities for artists in north Seattle.
